dependency_constraints.source: Used in the reproducer: `import numpy as np` and `np.random.default_rng`, `np.append`, `np.column_stack`, `np.isnan`.
Used in the reproducer: `from scipy import stats` and reference values via `stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum()`; PR text references `scipy's log_ndtr`/`norm.logcdf`/`norm.logpdf`.
Used as `import statsmodels.api as sm` and `sm.Probit(y, X)`; PR/issue refer to tests like `pytest statsmodels/discrete/tests`.

numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For extreme linear predictors (q*XB below about -8), Probit log-likelihood is computed as log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1)), producing a flat constant contribution log(eps) = -36.04 instead of the falling log(Phi(z)); the score uses the same clipped cdf in the Mills ratio so extreme observations contribute ~0 instead of a value growing like |z|; hessian/hessian_factor return nan below about z = -38. In the provided example, this yields wrong llf (-155.934 vs exact -1924.904), wrong-signed score ([-4.874, 7.393] vs exact [-64.891, -2393.273]), nan Hessian entries (np.isnan(...).any() == True), and bfgs fit ending at spurious params with nan bse (params [-0.036, 1.72], bse [nan, nan], llf -155.067 vs exact optimum params [-0.129, 0.077], llf -202.674).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Compute log-likelihood as log(Phi(z)) without clipping (use log_ndtr(z) instead of log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1))), compute Mills ratio in stable log space (exp(logpdf(z) - log_ndtr(z))) so inverse Mills ratio remains finite, and therefore avoid wrong llf/score sign and avoid nan Hessian for extreme z.
trigger_conditions: q * XB below about -8 (extreme misclassified observation) causes log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1)) to be flat at log(eps) = -36.04 instead of continuing to fall
hessian and hessian_factor do not clip and return nan below about z = -38
a single extreme, misclassified observation in the sample (via appending x=40.0 and y=0)
running Probit fit with gradient-based optimizer such as fit(method="bfgs") can stop at spurious points due to wrong-signed score

input_output_examples.input: params = [0.0, 1.5] on model Probit(y, X) where n=300, x = rng.standard_normal(300) with rng seed 1, y = (1.5*x + rng.standard_normal(n) > 0).astype(int), then x = append(x, 40.0), y = append(y, 0), and X = column_stack([ones(n+1), x]).
Same setup as above, res = model.fit(method="bfgs", disp=0).

oracle_clues: Problem statement quantifies the expected difference: log(Phi(z)) keeps falling (e.g., -53.2 at z=-10 and -804.6 at z=-40) while clipped computation is flat at log(eps) = -36.04 when q*XB below about -8.
Reference expected values in the repro are explicitly provided as “exact” for loglike, score, and the optimum llf/params for the given constructed dataset.

Correctness judgment uses scipy’s log_ndtr/norm.logcdf and norm.logpdf/logpdf parts (per PR description), and derivative checks against scipy references; bfgs should converge to the same optimum as direct scipy.optimize.minimize of the exact log-likelihood with finite bse.

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Extreme linear predictor regimes: q*XB below about -8 (log(clip(cdf(z), eps, 1)) flat at log(eps)) and below about -38 (log(cdf(z)) underflows to -inf; hessian returns nan where q*XB < -38; also reproduction uses z spanning -1e4..1e4 and includes an extreme x=40.0 misclassified observation).
category_specific_evidence: compute Probit loglike, score and hessian in log space because Probit previously evaluated log(clip(cdf(z), eps, 1)), which is flat at log(eps) for q*XB below about -8 while log(Phi(z)) keeps falling
log(cdf(z)) underflows to -inf below about -38; hessian did not clip and returned nan below z = -38
with an extreme misclassified observation this gave a wrong llf, a wrong-signed score, a nan Hessian and spurious bfgs optima with nan bse
The hessian is nan at any params where some q*XB < -38 (stated in issue reproduction discussion)
Reference/stable quantities are scipy's log_ndtr/norm.logcdf and norm.logpdf; match to R's pnorm(log.p=TRUE) and dnorm(log=TRUE) (PR description)
Test note: log_ndtr-based computation is exact and agrees with the stable reference; score_obs and hessian are asserted finite for z in [-1e4, 1e4] (test description)

Issue reproduction prints model.loglike(params) = -155.934 vs stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum() = -1924.904; model.score(params) = [-4.874  7.393] vs exact = [-64.891  -2393.273]; np.isnan(model.hessian(params)).any() = True
Issue reproduction after fit(method='bfgs'): res.params = [-0.036  1.72], res.bse = [nan nan], res.llf = -155.067 vs exact optimum params = [-0.129  0.077], llf = -202.674 (printed values)
reproduction_risks: If the extreme linear predictor regime is not triggered (e.g., q*XB not below about -8 and -38), the numerical pathology (flat loglike, underflow to -inf, nan Hessian) may not appear.

Using the same data construction (including x=40.0 appended and y appended with 0) and method/parameters (Probit, params=[0.0,1.5]) affects whether the incorrect llf/score/hessian NaNs and spurious bfgs optimum with nan bse are reproduced.

Omitting comparisons against the stable reference (stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum() and Mills ratio via log_ndtr/logpdf-log_ndtr) may hide the mathematical violation even if the model output is numerically unstable.

provenance.value: For extreme linear predictors (q*XB below about -8), Probit log-likelihood is computed as log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1)), producing a flat constant contribution log(eps) = -36.04 instead of the falling log(Phi(z)); the score uses the same clipped cdf in the Mills ratio so extreme observations contribute ~0 instead of a value growing like |z|; hessian/hessian_factor return nan below about z = -38. In the provided example, this yields wrong llf (-155.934 vs exact -1924.904), wrong-signed score ([-4.874, 7.393] vs exact [-64.891, -2393.273]), nan Hessian entries (np.isnan(...).any() == True), and bfgs fit ending at spurious params with nan bse (params [-0.036, 1.72], bse [nan, nan], llf -155.067 vs exact optimum params [-0.129, 0.077], llf -202.674).

Compute log-likelihood as log(Phi(z)) without clipping (use log_ndtr(z) instead of log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1))), compute Mills ratio in stable log space (exp(logpdf(z) - log_ndtr(z))) so inverse Mills ratio remains finite, and therefore avoid wrong llf/score sign and avoid nan Hessian for extreme z.

Extreme linear predictor regimes: q*XB below about -8 (log(clip(cdf(z), eps, 1)) flat at log(eps)) and below about -38 (log(cdf(z)) underflows to -inf; hessian returns nan where q*XB < -38; also reproduction uses z spanning -1e4..1e4 and includes an extreme x=40.0 misclassified observation).
